scope: Point-in-time read-only Docker, PostgreSQL and Flashscore queue capacity snapshot

prior_capacity_trial.outcome: aborted_resource_threshold; restored two browser processes; no sustained throughput improvement proven

interpretation: PostgreSQL is below its memory and connection limits. Its cache hit ratio is 97.94%; the point-in-time CPU sample is below its two-vCPU quota. No persistent lock wait was observed on follow-up.

Flashscore worker CPU is at its 1.5-vCPU quota in this sample. Increasing browser processes adds pressure on a saturated CPU quota and the prior four-process trial approached the worker memory threshold.
Most current PBP jobs are waiting for source identity or historical match indexing, not for a browser slot. The network slot gate was idle at this sample.
Redis and collector are closer to their memory caps than PostgreSQL and merit separate monitoring.
limitations: This is a point-in-time snapshot, not a sustained CPU or latency profile.
A transient lock waiter was visible in the first query, but a follow-up query found no blocked backend; lock contention is not established.
This report does not identify top PostgreSQL statements; pg_stat_statements is not installed.
Live Chromium root-process count was not available from this sample.
